newsitem.title: UK: Funds turn positive on Japan equities - Merrill poll.
newsitem.headline: Funds turn positive on Japan equities - Merrill poll.

text.p: Sentiment towards Japanese markets has shown a substantial recovery since the beginning of the year with domestic and foreign fund managers keen to increase their exposure in the region, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.
"While managers appear to be reluctant to raise their weightings to equity markets generally, they are making an exception for Japan," Merrill said in its global fund manager survey for May.
It said the confidence most likely flowed from increasing optimism on the Japanese economy.
Japanese fund managers' investment preferences reflect an upbeat view on the economy, with buyers outnumbering sellers by 45 percent -- a level not seen since the spring of 1996.
Sellers of Japanese bonds also increased in May from April.
Among the Tokyo Stock Exchange sectors, managers prefer manufacturing and are not keen on financials.
The survey said Asia Pacific managers were overweighting Hong Kong in favour of Australia, with the two coming in nine percent overweight and nine percent underweight respectively.
But it said the underweight Australian position could be changing, with 29 percent more buyers than sellers in the region in May.
The survey of Japanese fund managers was carried out by Gallup on behalf of Merrill between may 5 and 6, covering 45 institutions responsible for funds totalling $530 billion.
